chapter: Lecture 5: Weathering of Rocks and Minerals — Types, Physical & Biological Agents
subject: agricultural_chemistry_and_soil_science

questions.stem: A 1 m³ solid rock cube is progressively subdivided down to colloidal clay dimensions (1 µm). Which mathematical and geochemical statements are correct? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Total exposed surface area expands from 6 m² up to 6,000,000 m² (6 km²).
options.B: Specific surface area increases inversely with particle edge dimension (S ∝ 1/l).
options.C: Chemical dissolution reaction velocity increases by orders of magnitude due to abundant reactive atomic sites.
options.D: Total mass and mineral volume decrease to zero.
options.E: The expanding surface area provides extensive negative charge sites for nutrient cation adsorption.

questions.rationale: Pulverizing a 1m cube (6 m²) to 1 µm yields 6,000,000 m² (a 1,000,000-fold expansion); S ∝ 1/l; reaction rates surge; cation exchange sites multiply. Mass and volume are conserved. (Key Takeaway: Colloidal subdivision creates 6 km² of reactive surface area per cubic meter.)

questions.stem: Why does polymineralic Granite undergo granular disintegration under diurnal thermal cycling? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Quartz grains expand cubically at twice (2.0x) the rate of adjacent feldspar grains during solar heating.
options.B: Dark biotite and hornblende crystals absorb solar radiation faster, enduring sharper thermal stress than leucocratic minerals.
options.C: Differential volumetric expansion sets up intense microscopic shear stresses along intergranular crystal boundaries.
options.D: Repeated diurnal expansion and contraction weakens intergranular cohesion, causing individual mineral grains to dislodge.
options.E: Granite expands linearly at ten times the rate of sandstone.

questions.rationale: Quartz expands 2x vs feldspar; dark minerals heat faster; differential expansion generates intergranular shear stress, causing granular disintegration. Granite linear expansion is 0.5x sandstone, not 10x. (Key Takeaway: Differential thermal expansion between quartz and feldspar drives granular disintegration in granite.)

questions.stem: In comparing the weathering dynamics of river systems from headwaters to mouth, which statements are scientifically valid? (Select all that apply)

options.A: River headwaters have high stream gradients that generate velocities capable of transporting cobbles (1.2 m/s) and boulders (9.0 m/s).
options.B: Coarse, angular suspended clasts in headwaters act as abrasive cutting tools against exposed bedrock.
options.C: Near the river mouth, reduced stream velocity causes sediment deposition rather than bedrock abrasion.
options.D: Disintegration of rock clasts is substantially greater near the source of a river than near its mouth.
options.E: River mouths exhibit zero dissolved chemical ions.

questions.rationale: Headwater velocities (1.2–9.0 m/s), angular bedload abrasion, downstream deposition, and source-dominated disintegration gradients are verified fluvial laws. River mouths carry high dissolved ions. (Key Takeaway: High velocity and coarse bedload make headwaters zones of intense mechanical disintegration.)

questions.stem: Which biogeochemical processes occur when living plant roots interact with rock minerals in the rhizosphere? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Root radial turgor pressure mechanically splits rock joints and microfissures.
options.B: Root exudates containing citric, oxalic, and malic acids lower rhizosphere pH and chelate polyvalent metal cations.
options.C: Decomposing root channels leave open macropores that conduct surface rainwater and atmospheric CO₂ deep into saprolite.
options.D: Rhizosphere respiration raises soil air CO₂ levels, generating carbonic acid for silicate hydrolysis.
options.E: Plant roots convert all rock silica into pure elemental gaseous carbon.

questions.rationale: Mechanical turgor wedging, organic acid chelation, decayed root macropores, and elevated carbonic acid are fundamental rhizosphere processes. Silica is not converted to gaseous carbon. (Key Takeaway: The rhizosphere combines turgor wedging, organic chelation, percolation macropores, and carbonic acid attack.)

questions.stem: What specific roles do subterranean Ants and Termites perform in the weathering of tropical and subtropical soils? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Pedoturbation: Excavating fine mineral grains from deep saprolite horizons and depositing them in surface mounds.
options.B: Constructing extensive gallery networks that enhance deep rainwater percolation and aeration.
options.C: Secreting concentrated biochemical formic acid (HCOOH) that chemically corrodes and etches silicate mineral lattices.
options.D: Concentrating organic matter and nutrients within termite mounds, accelerating localized biochemical decomposition.

questions.rationale: Termites and ants execute pedoturbation, build percolation galleries, secrete corrosive formic acid, and concentrate organic matter. They do not produce magma. (Key Takeaway: Termites and ants drive physical pedoturbation, percolation gallery formation, and formic acid corrosion.)

questions.stem: Under what climatic and geomorphic conditions is Frost Wedging (Cryofracturing) the dominant physical weathering engine? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Alpine mountain summits and periglacial zones experiencing frequent diurnal freeze-thaw cycles across 0°C.
options.B: Bedrock with open joint networks and microscopic fissures accessible to liquid water.
options.C: Environments where liquid water freezes in confined spaces, expanding by 9% and exerting 1465 Mg m⁻² bursting pressure.
options.D: Hyper-arid tropical deserts with nighttime temperatures consistently above 30°C.
options.E: High-latitude cliffs where frost shatter produces extensive angular talus/scree slopes.

questions.rationale: Alpine freeze-thaw cycles, open joint networks, 9% ice expansion exerting 1465 Mg m⁻², and talus slope formation characterize cryofracture. Tropical deserts above 30°C do not experience frost wedging. (Key Takeaway: Alpine diurnal freeze-thaw cycles and 1465 Mg m⁻² bursting pressure drive cryofracturing.)

questions.stem: Which statements accurately reflect the differences between primary minerals and secondary minerals in soil science? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Primary minerals (quartz, feldspars, micas, pyroxenes) formed at high temperatures/pressures in igneous and metamorphic rocks.
options.B: Secondary minerals (kaolinite, smectite, gibbsite, goethite) are synthesized at low surface temperatures during weathering.
options.C: Primary silicate minerals are thermodynamically unstable when exposed to surface water and oxygen.
options.D: Secondary clay minerals possess high surface area and cation exchange capacity crucial for crop nutrition.
options.E: Secondary minerals are formed exclusively in deep magmatic magma chambers.

questions.rationale: Primary minerals form under deep igneous/metamorphic conditions and are unstable at the surface; secondary clays/oxides are synthesized at surface conditions and supply CEC. Secondary minerals do not form in magma. (Key Takeaway: Secondary clays and sesquioxides are low-temperature weathering synthesis products.)

questions.stem: Why is the v⁶ wind carrying capacity power law critical in geomorphology and soil erosion? (Select all that apply)

options.A: A slight increase in wind velocity causes a massive exponential surge in sediment transport capacity.
options.B: Doubling wind velocity increases potential kinetic sediment carrying power by a factor of 64 (2⁶ = 64).
options.C: Tripling wind velocity increases transport capacity by a factor of 729 (3⁶ = 729).
options.D: Strong gale-force desert winds can transport vast volumes of abrasive sand, causing rapid eolian sandblasting.
options.E: Wind velocity has zero mathematical impact on sediment transport.

questions.rationale: The v⁶ power law dictates that transport capacity increases by 2⁶ = 64x for double speed and 3⁶ = 729x for triple speed, explaining extreme storm sandblasting. (Key Takeaway: The v^6 power law causes carrying capacity to surge exponentially with wind speed.)

questions.stem: How does Anthropogenic activity (Man) alter natural geomorphic weathering rates? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Explosive rock blasting pulverizes solid lithological strata in seconds.
options.B: Open-cast mining and deep quarrying expose deep unweathered bedrock to surface atmospheric water and oxygen.
options.C: Heavy machinery excavation for highways, railways, and dams fragments hillsides at industrial scale.
options.D: Industrial acid precipitation (acid rain) accelerates chemical decomposition of building stones and natural outcrops.
options.E: Human activity has completely eliminated all natural physical and chemical weathering processes globally.

questions.rationale: Blasting, mining, engineering excavation, and acid rain accelerate weathering rates by orders of magnitude. Human activity does not eliminate natural weathering. (Key Takeaway: Anthropogenic blasting, mining, and acid rain vastly accelerate lithospheric weathering rates.)

questions.stem: Which physical and chemical factors determine why massive Granite weathers into rounded boulders and exfoliation domes? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Granite is a massive, homogeneous plutonic rock with widely spaced orthogonal joints.
options.B: Diurnal heating and cooling causes outer rock shells to expand and contract while the interior remains cool, causing exfoliation.
options.C: Corners and edges of rectangular joint blocks weather from multiple faces simultaneously, rounding the blocks (spheroidal weathering).
options.D: Quartz grains resist chemical hydrolysis, preserving the structural core of the rock mass.
options.E: Granite is soluble in water like pure rock salt.

questions.rationale: Homogeneous structure, thermal exfoliation spalling, corner rounding (spheroidal weathering), and quartz chemical resistance shape rounded granite domes. Granite is not water-soluble like halite. (Key Takeaway: Thermal exfoliation, joint spacing, and corner rounding create rounded granite domes.)
